name: buffers until explicit flush below capacity
input: write two chunks smaller than the capacity
test:
class Sink:
    def __init__(self): self.writes = []
    def write(self, data): self.writes.append(data)
sink = Sink()
writer = BufferedFileWriter(sink, 5)
writer.write(b'ab')
writer.write(b'cd')
assert sink.writes == []
writer.flush()
assert sink.writes == [b'abcd']

name: automatically flushes exactly when the buffer fills
input: writes combine to exactly the capacity
test:
class Sink:
    def __init__(self): self.writes = []
    def write(self, data): self.writes.append(data)
sink = Sink()
writer = BufferedFileWriter(sink, 4)
writer.write(b'ab')
writer.write(b'cd')
assert sink.writes == [b'abcd']
writer.flush()
assert sink.writes == [b'abcd']

name: chunks writes larger than capacity and preserves residual data
input: one write spans multiple full buffers and a remainder
test:
class Sink:
    def __init__(self): self.writes = []
    def write(self, data): self.writes.append(data)
sink = Sink()
writer = BufferedFileWriter(sink, 3)
writer.write(b'abcdefgh')
assert sink.writes == [b'abc', b'def']
assert all(len(chunk) <= 3 for chunk in sink.writes)
writer.flush()
assert sink.writes == [b'abc', b'def', b'gh']

name: combines consecutive writes and flushes the residual bytes
input: several writes fill the buffer more than once, then explicit flush
test:
class Sink:
    def __init__(self): self.writes = []
    def write(self, data): self.writes.append(data)
sink = Sink()
writer = BufferedFileWriter(sink, 4)
writer.write(b'a')
writer.write(b'bc')
writer.write(b'defghi')
assert sink.writes == [b'abcd', b'efgh']
writer.flush()
assert sink.writes == [b'abcd', b'efgh', b'i']
